subject: Order Form indemnity: proposed handback & evidence timing
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@solara-systems.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@procureco.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form indemnity: proposed handback & evidence timing

Hi Elena / Daniel —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As discussed, Solara is asking for a narrower handback/notice path in the Order Form when third-party IP claims arise from model output. We captured a working proposal in the attached redlines (redlines_v2.docx) and an evidence matrix that maps what Solara would reasonably request from us vs. what the customer must preserve (evidence_matrix.xlsx).

High-level proposal we sent:
- Redwood accepts defense/control for third-party infringement claims tied to our hosted models but only where the claim relates to the base model weights and not customer prompts or customer-submitted training data.
- If we accept defense, Solara must provide timely technical artifacts (sample inputs, logs, prompt history) within the notice window; failure to do so shifts responsibility back to Solara.
- If Solara insists on a broader handback, we want an explicit 30-day cure/evidence window and a cap on fees related to preservation requests.

Can you review the attached and let us know the must-haves from legal/procurement on your side? We’d like to land language that: (a) preserves our ability to route claims to insurer/defense counsel, (b) sets clear timelines for evidence, and (c) minimizes open-ended discovery-style preservation asks.

If you’re open, we can propose an alternate two-paragraph Order Form addendum that codifies the handback/evidence timeline and a mutual escalation contact.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Mina —

Thanks for the note and the docs. Quick clarifying points from Solara Legal:
1) The definition of "model output" — we want to confirm Solara is not on the hook for outputs generated by Redwood’s fine-tuned variants if Redwood applied downstream modifications without Solara’s input.
2) Evidence window — 30 days seems short for some of our regulated workflows. Can we do 60 days for preservation but have mutually agreed tiers where urgent evidence (logs + sample input) is due in 14 days?
3) Caps — we are OK with limiting broad preservation costs, but request an explicit bucket for reasonable third-party forensic fees.

We can take a pass at your two-paragraph addendum if you send the draft. Also looping procurement (Daniel) to confirm whether the Order Form signature cadence needs any separate approval cycles on our side.

Elena
Elena Morales
VP Legal, Solara Systems

Mina / team —

Quick draft positions below (high level). I put proposed contract text into the redlines_v2.docx (see track changes). Main points:

- Scope (model output): add a short definition: "Model Output" means text, images, or other content produced by a Redwood-hosted model instance or officially distributed model artifact provided to Customer as part of the Services; excludes Customer-provided prompts, customer-supplied training data, or third-party integrations not operated by Redwood.

- Defense/evidence handback: two-tier timeline: "Urgent Evidence" = logs and sample inputs due within 14 days of written notice; "Full Preservation" = all requested artifacts due within 60 days unless Redwood reasonably object in writing. Failure to provide timely evidence will permit Redwood to decline defense and limit liability to reimbursement only.

- Preservation costs cap: Redwood will cover reasonable preservation costs up to $25,000 total per claim; any additional costs require prior written consent and will be split 50/50. We propose adding a requirement that any forensic vendor be mutually agreed or on a pre-approved vendor list.

- Escalation/contacts: include a mutual escalation path with specific SLA (72 hours for acknowledgement, 10 business days for initial triage report).

Open questions for Ops/CS (Jordan / Ben):
1) Is the 14d/60d timeline operationally feasible for hosted customers? If not, what are the realistic target windows?
2) For evidence types that require retrieval from cold storage (long-term archives), can we define a separate cold-retrieval SLA and cost bucket?

If Jordan/Ben confirm operational feasibility, I recommend we send this language back to Solara with a short cover note offering the two-paragraph addendum for quick incorporation into the Order Form.

-Kimberly

All —

Ops check: 14d for logs/sample inputs is OK for hosted flows where we have live KV/cache and request logging enabled. 60d for full preservation is borderline but doable with the following constraints:
- Cold retrieval may take 7–10 business days and we should have a separate fee estimate (we can provide an estimate to Solara).
- We need a single point of contact at Solara that can authorize retrievals; without that we can get stuck.
- For forensic vendor requests, we prefer to own initial triage and only involve external vendors with mutual sign-off.

Ben will produce a short ops FAQ for sales that maps evidence categories to expected retrieval effort/cost. If legal is comfortable with the $25k cap, we can accept conditional language that allows additional costs with prior consent.

Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity: proposed handback & evidence timing

Elena / Solara team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Attached is a slightly revised addendum and the evidence matrix annotated with ops notes and estimated cold-retrieval costs. Short summary of our compromise positions:

- We’ll keep the defense carve tied to Redwood-hosted model defects and explicitly exclude customer prompts and customer-supplied training data. We will, however, accept responsibility for our downstream fine-tuned variants only when the fine-tuning was performed and controlled by Redwood (not customer-managed fine-tuning).
- Two-tier evidence timeline: 14 days for urgent artifacts (logs + sample inputs) and 60 days for full preservation. Cold-retrieval fees and timelines will be listed in the evidence matrix; Redwood will cover up to $25,000 of preservation/costs per claim, with excess subject to prior written consent.
- We’ll add an SLA for acknowledgement (72 hours) and an initial triage report within 10 business days.

If this is acceptable, we can submit the tracked redline to Solara Legal for confirmation and prepare a one-page addendum to attach to the Order Form for signature. Daniel — please confirm the procurement path (single sign-off vs. multi-approver) so we can align timing.

Next steps:
1) Solara to confirm the $25k cap and the 14/60 windows (or propose alternatives) by EOD 10/20.
2) Redwood to prepare final two-paragraph addendum and clean redline for Solara counsel.
3) Ops to publish a 1-pager for Sales referencing the evidence matrix and cost buckets.

Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
